candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — interpretation of peak-flow monitoring
candidate.educational_objective: Use percentage of personal-best peak expiratory flow to identify the CDC asthma-action-plan red zone and respond according to the individualized plan.

options.A: It is in the red-zone medical-alert range and the client should follow the red-zone instructions in the individualized asthma action plan.
options.B: It is in the green zone because any peak flow above 40% of personal best indicates good control.
options.C: It is in the yellow zone because readings from 40% through 80% of personal best are managed the same way.
options.D: Peak-flow percentage is unrelated to asthma action plans and should be ignored if the client currently feels well.

candidate.rationale: The CDC Asthma Action Plan places peak flow less than half of the client's best peak flow in the red-zone medical-alert category. A reading of 45% of personal best therefore falls in the red zone and should trigger the client's prescribed red-zone action-plan instructions. The CDC green zone is more than 80% of best peak flow, while the yellow zone is approximately one-half to three-quarters of best peak flow. Current symptoms do not negate a red-zone peak-flow reading in a plan that uses peak flow.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC's current asthma action plan classifies peak flow less than half of personal best as a red-zone medical alert and directs the client to follow prescribed red-zone actions and contact the clinician, with hospital care if symptoms do not improve and the clinician cannot be reached.
candidate.source_document_title: Living with Asthma — Asthma Action Plans
candidate.source_locator: Asthma Action Plans > Green Zone, Yellow Zone, Red Zone: red-zone peak flow is less than half of personal best; yellow is half to about three-quarters; green is more than 80% or more of best peak flow
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A client with asthma uses a peak-flow meter and obtains a reading that is 45% of the client's personal-best peak flow. According to the CDC Asthma Action Plan, how should the nurse interpret this finding?
